links.outcome: False positive and false negative rates by race at standard 0.5 threshold
links.effect: FPR 27.71% for Black vs 5.92% for White patients (factor 4.68); FNR 43.11% vs 73.82% (factor 0.58); FPR/FNR 8 times higher for Black patients.
links.quote: These statistics demonstrate that the models are biased and are more likely to classify Black patients as belonging to the very high SBP group.

links.outcome: Effect of race-specific decision thresholds on error-rate parity between Black and White patients
links.effect: Thresholds of 0.296 (Black) and 0.245 (White) equalized FNR at 25%; FPR became 41.11% vs 47.20%; FPR/FNR ratio factor 0.87 versus ~8 before. Weighted F1 fell to 65.77% and 60.91%.
links.quote: The resulting FPR of the model for Black patients becomes 41.11% and the FPR for White patient model becomes 47.20%.

links.outcome: Influence of race as a model input on predictions and bias
links.effect: Race_Black was the third most important feature (OR 1.94, CI 1.90-1.98); the non-stratified model showed implicit racial disparity.
links.quote: We found implicit racial disparity in the non-stratified predictive model.
